evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is self-contained and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: give them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by giving a game URL inherently requires a game (and its URL) to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: start a round
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes that a game/session exists to start the round in.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the session's items requires those items to have been added or created in prior stories (items/rounds).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires that items exist (have been added or created in a round) beforehand.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items is scoped to a game/session and therefore requires a game to exist.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires that the item (and list) already exists (created via add/start round).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires that item(s) exist in the list (added or created earlier).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates presupposes that a round/estimates exist (round/estimation functionality must be in place).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates have been collected in a round, so it depends on round/estimation functionality.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling the estimate depends on estimators showing cards and the round/estimation mechanism being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate assumes a negotiated estimate for an item after a round, so it depends on rounds/items existing.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating an earlier story inherently requires that story to have been estimated earlier in the session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires that previous games exist (created/stored by game creation and play).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript requires that a game and its rounds/estimates have been played and recorded.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires the transcript-viewing/recording capability to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript presupposes that transcripts are available (viewing/recording implemented).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game requires games to exist in storage (created previously).

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Creating an account is self-contained and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires an account to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presupposes an existing account.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires that the account exists.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone presentation is a standalone presentation feature and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders require that an account with an email exists.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selection of estimation scale is a standalone settings feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators is tied to a specific game/session and therefore requires a game to exist.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a received URL presupposes that an invitation/URL has been generated (the invite feature).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires that a round/item has been started or selected.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the session's items requires those items to have been added or created.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Noticing that an estimator has given an estimate depends on the estimation/round mechanics being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates is inherently tied to the round/estimation process and needs that functionality.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: Changing estimates during a draw presupposes the draw/estimation mechanics are implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates requires storage/access to previous rounds/estimates (history/browsing prior rounds).

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Seeing per-estimator estimates in a round depends on the estimation/reveal mechanism that shows estimates.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Auto-resetting the timer depends on the timer existing and the estimation detection (timer and estimate mechanics).

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Browsing prior rounds requires that prior rounds and estimates exist (round/item creation and storage).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering is a standalone UI/behavior feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Ability to change estimates during a draw presupposes the draw/estimation mechanism is in place.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail presumes user/profile photo data exists (accounts/profile capability).

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a standalone non-functional requirement and not inherently dependent on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating definitions is self-contained and does not require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing is an implementation task not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser support is a standalone quality requirement and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a non-functional requirement and is self-contained regarding dependencies.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance expectation is a standalone quality requirement and not inherently dependent on another story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a standalone capability and does not inherently require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a self-contained requirement and not inherently dependent on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is self-contained and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Data anonymization is a storage/privacy requirement and does not inherently require another specific backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics can be implemented as a standalone feature; while they consume game data, they do not explicitly require another backlog story to be implemented first.
